as_told.title: Malmgren in the Cuban Missile Crisis war room confronts Curtis LeMay

plain: An analyst named Matthew Pines tells a podcast host, Jesse Michels, that during the 1962 Cuban missile crisis a young advisor, Harold Malmgren, was sent by President John F. Kennedy into the tank, a secure Pentagon meeting room for top commanders, to stall Air Force General Curtis LeMay and keep him from possibly using nuclear weapons. Malmgren himself tells it firsthand, saying he argued that striking Moscow would be madness because it would leave no one to negotiate with, and he names defense officials Robert McNamara and McGeorge Bundy as present. Told this way, it would mean Malmgren helped hold back a nuclear war.
